chunks: Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated to us, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:

When al-Qa'im (peace be upon him) rises, the angels of Badr will descend. They are five thousand angels. A third of them will be on gray horses, a third on piebald horses, and a third on red horses. I asked: And what is 'al-haww'? He said: It is the donkeys.
ai.seo_question: What are the angels of Badr and what are their mounts according to the hadith of al-Qa'im?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani highlights the eschatological sign of the angels of Badr descending to support al-Qa'im, mirroring the divine assistance granted to the Prophet at the Battle of Badr. The specific mention of five thousand angels and their varied mounts (including donkeys, or 'al-haww') underscores the supernatural nature of the Mahdi's victory. This event is viewed in Shia tradition as the fulfillment of divine promise, where celestial forces actively intervene to establish justice.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (44) Abu Sulayman Ahmad bin Hawtha narrated from Ibraheem bin Iss’haq an-Nahawandi from Abdullah bin Hammad al-Ansari from Ali bin Abu Hamza that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said:
“When al-Qa’im (as) rises, the angels of Badr will descend. They are five thousand angels. A third of them will be on gray horses, a third on piebald horses and a third on red horses.”
